# Open311 service reporting

Operate a saved service-reporting desk from complete Open311 collection exports. The desk supports named creation periods, explicit observation cutoffs, service mappings, working calendars, internal targets, management commentary and source-linked reviewer returns.

Start with the installed [operating and receiving guide](INSTALL.md). The [source contract](SOURCE_CONTRACT.md) explains the supported provider timestamp meanings and reporting rules.

## A complete operator workflow

1. Collect the original service requests through the installed Open311 collection workspace, including all refined windows and source responses.
2. Import its complete collection JSON. The reporting desk retains the exact incoming file, original workspace/revision/collection identity, complete source bytes, all observations and source-linked review history.
3. Save an immutable reporting profile. Name the provider semantics, service mappings, calendar editions, target policies and the local interpretation of any date-only review deadline.
4. Select a creation period using an explicit start and exclusive end. Freeze the observation cutoff and source/profile editions. Review the source coverage and unmapped services.
5. Build the report. Source status, internal review state, reporting groups and selected targets remain distinct in every request drilldown. Percentages include their eligible numerator and denominator.
6. Download the management HTML, spreadsheet CSV, full report package or reviewer-return template.
7. Receive the full package in a new private reporting workspace. All report/source editions and original operation histories travel together. The receiving workspace has its own identity and can continue the report series.
8. Import a reviewer return, compare any intervening report edition and select the individual changes to incorporate. The resulting successor retains its original source pins and reviewer history.

## Calendar and target choices

The [weekday review profile](examples/weekday-review-profile.json) is a complete operator configuration accepted by the CLI and browser. It defines a TJLabs internal review target of 240 working minutes, with weekday hours 09:00–17:00 in Europe/Helsinki. The operator can choose another calendar, target or clock origin before saving an edition.

Calendars use weekday keys 0=Sunday through 6=Saturday. Each local interval has start/end values in HH:mm; 24:00 is supported as an end. A date override replaces the whole local date, including an empty array for a closure. Represent overnight work on its two local dates.

Working time is resolved separately for each date. A repeated daylight-saving boundary requires an explicit earlier/later choice; a nonexistent boundary needs an actual date override. Each report saves its resolved UTC intervals, complete policy/calendar editions and calculation runtime. Reading an existing report uses the saved calculations.

Mapping and target rules use exact selectors and an explicit integer priority. The highest-priority matching rule applies. Equal-priority matches appear as a calculation issue requiring an operator choice. A service priority label acquires a duration only through a named target policy.

## Source and report identities

Source import identity is the original workspace ID, original revision and collection ID. The complete incoming file also has a SHA-256. Identical imports reuse the existing source edition. An alternate file for an already retained identity produces a visible conflict.

Each report names its source editions, profile edition, observation cutoff, period, filters and selected target basis. A request first observed after the cutoff is counted as unobserved at that time. Limited source windows contribute their observed rows and retain their exact unresolved boundaries in coverage.

The supported provider profiles are `helsinki` and `georeport-v2`. Helsinki READY/PROCESSING values describe source processing state; its last-update timestamp remains a last update. Under GeoReport v2 semantics, a closed request's update time can supply closure duration. A missing or invalid target remains unassessed.

## Saved review changes

A reviewer-return file names its exact base report ID/SHA-256 and reviewer. Each change has a stable ID, a kind and commentary:

- `report-comment`: commentary for the complete report.
- `request-comment`: commentary with the original request key and source-version SHA-256.

The desk retains the complete return file. An operator selects the change IDs to incorporate. If the series has moved, the desk shows the comparison and requires the chosen current edition. A source-version change stays visible before a request comment can be linked to that newer source.

## Operation and receiving behavior

All mutations carry a stable request ID and expected workspace revision. The saved original request supports lookup after a dropped response. Repeating the same action returns its existing result; a changed action cannot silently reuse its ID. The browser retains large original commands in IndexedDB, supports download and offers recovery before another action.

HTML escapes source text. CSV protects spreadsheet formula text. The complete JSON package contains the source files, normalized records, report editions, configuration, review returns, current operation history and received original operation histories. Receiving validates those original bytes and references before writing one transaction to an empty destination.

The local server is private to its selected loopback address. Its Applications launcher verifies the workspace identity, directory binding and live server instance before opening the desk.

# Open311 reporting source and operating contract

This document defines the reporting workbench that consumes the original immutable collection export. Reporting owns its saved calendars, target policies, mappings, report editions and reviewer comments. Acquisition and its original capture history remain with the collection workspace.

## Primary sources

1. [Open311 GeoReport v2](https://wiki.open311.org/GeoReport_v2/), GET Service Requests and GET Service Request.
2. [Helsinki feedback service API, 1 October 2025](https://www.hel.fi/static/avoindata/kanslia/Open311_API_description_011025.pdf), pages 3 and 6–9.
3. [FixMyStreet public Open311 interface](https://www.fixmystreet.com/open311).
4. [SocietyWorks FixMyStreet Pro administrator manual](https://fixmystreet.org/pro-manual/admin-tasks/), priorities, statistics, data export and automatic dashboard import.
5. [SocietyWorks integrations, assets and data](https://www.societyworks.org/features/integrations/).

The following implementation choices are our reporting contract. Provider facts are identified by source number.

## 1. Immutable input

Accept the complete `commons.open311.collection-export.v1` envelope:

```text
workspaceId, revision, collection, summary, requests,
observations, originals, sourceOperations
```

The collection preserves its frozen connection, attribution, plan and all windows. Summary contains counts, capResolved and first/last observation times. Each selected request retains captureId, sourceSha256 and its separate review. Observations preserve selectedCaptureId, all occurrences and every distinct original item/hash. An occurrence carries captureId, windowId, capturedAt, sourceSha256, sourceResponseSha256, windowPosition, requestedAt and updatedAt. Originals contain complete raw responses, including capped parent captures.

Import by a complete-envelope digest plus original workspace/revision/collection identity. A repeated import of identical content reuses its edition. Preserve the incoming selected item and all alternative versions. Reject a conflicting payload for an already retained exact identity. Original source remains immutable; operator category mappings and commentary are separate saved records.

Reports count each original request key once in their selected cohort. Capture occurrences and distinct source versions have separate counts. Preserve original null, empty and vendor-specific values. A missing service code belongs to an explicit unmapped group unless an operator has supplied a named mapping.

## 2. Status and time semantics

GeoReport v2 defines open and closed. requested_datetime is creation time; updated_datetime is the latest change and, for a closed request, the closure time. expected_datetime is optional and describes the expected fulfilment time, potentially from a service-specific SLA. Query start/end select creation time; each standard query spans at most 90 days. Timezone offsets are required. [1]

Helsinki documents processing-status values with PROCESSING and READY examples. Its updated_datetime means latest update; expected_datetime, agency_responsible and service_notice are unavailable. service_code and service_name apply when feedback was created through Open311. Its public search covers published feedback, with a stated 90-day/200-response return limit. [2]

Keep these contracts in named provider profiles. The standard profile may use closed-request updatedAt for resolution duration. Helsinki retains READY as a source status and updatedAt as latest update; any operational status grouping is a saved reporting mapping. A reporting mapping does not change the source timestamp meaning.

Store three independent target fields:

- sourceExpectedAt: the unchanged provider value, where valid.
- reviewDueAt: an existing operator review/assignment deadline.
- policyDueAt: the computed deadline from an explicitly selected target-policy edition.

The report names the selected comparison target. A missing target is counted as unassessed. A request with a valid zero duration remains valid; an invalid timestamp or reversed interval is retained with a specific calculation issue. Source status, review state and reporting bucket remain separate fields.

## 3. Periods, observation time and coverage

A named report period uses an explicit half-open interval [start,end), a display timezone and a cohort basis. The default cohort is requestedAt in that interval. These report boundaries are applied after acquisition and do not alter the provider's saved request URLs. The public FixMyStreet interface explicitly defines inclusive start_date and exclusive end_date. [3]

Freeze report asOf and the source edition selection. For historical selection, use the latest retained observation at or before asOf; an item first observed later is unobserved at that cutoff. A creation-period cohort can display its status from a later selected observation, provided that observation date is shown. It cannot automatically become a full historical end-of-period backlog.

Display the exact collection filters, observation interval, capResolved, all unresolved/limited window bounds and source row counts with the report. A LIMITED leaf contributes its returned rows to observed totals and remains visible in coverage. Source capture covers its selected query/filters and observation interval. Counting closure-time events across all older creation cohorts requires the appropriate source selection; a short creation-window capture alone does not supply them.

Saved comparisons pin both report editions. Cohort totals, mapping changes, missing targets, unmapped services, unresolved windows and distinct observation cutoffs remain visible. Percentages carry numerator and denominator. With an empty denominator, the value is unassessed, not zero.

## 4. Named calendars and target policies

Calendars are operator-owned configuration, independent of provider expected dates. Each immutable edition contains:

```text
id, name, revision, timeZone, weeklyIntervals,
dateOverrides, effectiveFrom, effectiveUntil, sourceReferences
```

Use valid IANA timezone names. Weekly intervals are local wall-clock working periods. Date overrides explicitly replace a date's intervals, including holidays/closures and exceptional opening. Preserve their original source or operator attribution.

Policies contain a stable ID/name/edition, the applicable saved service/agency/priority mapping, durationMinutes, clockMode (elapsed or business), calendar edition when required, and the chosen source/assignment clock origin. Require an explicit rule when more than one policy matches. Never extract a numeric target automatically from a priority label.

Elapsed minutes compare absolute UTC instants. Business minutes intersect the task interval with the selected local working intervals, converting each date's boundaries to UTC independently. Overnight work is represented as two dated intervals. Reject overlapping intervals, ambiguous/nonexistent local boundaries without an explicit resolution, and calendars with no reachable working time. A bare “business days” target needs an explicit definition before it is converted to minutes.

Each saved report retains the exact calendar/policy editions and resolved time intervals used. Reopening a report reproduces its arithmetic when host timezone data or an operator's current policy changes. Targets do not rewrite provider fields.

## 5. Customer workflow and export behavior

SocietyWorks' administrator manual describes council/ward/category/date/status filtering, grouping by category/state/month/device, CSV export of Reports or Updates, and category-specific priority names/descriptions/external IDs. Its dashboard CSV is generated overnight and excludes the current day. Automatic import uses the selected export URL and a token; export=1 waits for a file, while export=2 returns HTTP 202 with a redirect to the future file location. [4]

Accordingly, the reporting desk supports named selections, separate source/report/review states, mapped service groups, explicit source dates and saved management commentary. A future dashboard CSV import retains whether it is Reports or Updates, its actual response/export parameters and observation time; HTTP 202 is a pending export operation until the actual file is received. The initial workbench consumes the complete collection envelope above.

The management report presents intake counts, source-status groups, assigned/reviewed workload, age or valid resolution duration, chosen-target performance and exact request drilldowns. HTML and CSV are rendered from the same immutable report edition; JSON includes all calculations, policy/mapping editions, cohort membership and source references. Escape source text for HTML and protect spreadsheet text cells when rendering CSV.

A complete report package includes its original collection export and raw response inventory, report definition, calculations, calendars, mappings, commentary and operation history. Reviewer returns name the original report/base revision and source request/version for each change. Changed bases produce a visible comparison; the operator can retain or incorporate each returned change into a successor edition. Exact request IDs support recovery after a lost response.

## 6. Original-data receiving journey

Use the already retained full Helsinki source carrier (9,730 bytes, SHA256 88a4bbe75bc199de29627610862a720ce56aac644de04a558c4067d4602ed300) and the complete collection export created from that source.

Import; choose the actual creation period; inspect all source statuses, blank service/agency fields and unavailable provider expectations; save an explicit operator calendar and target policy; save commentary; produce the complete report formats; transfer to an independent reporting workspace; reopen the same report; return one source-linked review change and incorporate it into a successor. Keep the source values and original collection identity through the whole journey.

The useful arithmetic checks exercise the actual saved source plus explicit operator configuration: repeat import, request deduplication across overlapping captures, zero or missing denominators, an overnight/holiday boundary and report reproduction after a newer calendar edition. These are focused checks of the customer calculation and receiving behavior.

# Install and operate Open311 service-performance reporting

This product turns complete Open311 source collections into saved service reports. It carries the collection's original responses, window coverage, source versions and internal reviews into an independent reporting workspace. Operators save their own service mappings, calendars, targets and reporting periods, inspect each calculated result, compare reports, and exchange selected reviewer comments.

The installed selection includes both **Open311 municipal service operations** and **Open311 service performance** in merchant Applications. The acquisition workspace and reporting workspace use separate directories and SQLite files. A complete collection export is the explicit handover between them.

## Runtime and package

Use Node.js 22.13 or newer with its built-in SQLite support. Start the commands from an exact source checkout or from the installed merchant package. The reporting component adds no external database, subscription or hosted compute.

The maintained source selection is `open311-reporting`. Build it from the repository revision you intend to install:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo . \
  --ref EXACT_SOURCE_COMMIT \
  --selection open311-reporting \
  --out /absolute/new/open311-reporting-package \
  --offline
```

Choose a new output directory. The selection includes the original Open311 operations contribution, the independent reporting contribution, the maintained merchant host, and the source components required by those applications. The generated product uses the existing `starforge` command. In an installed environment, its reporting command is `starforge open311-reporting`; its source-acquisition command is `starforge open311`.

The examples below use the direct source entrypoint so every path is explicit:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs --help
```

The package exports the reporting SDK as `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-reporting` and its workspace API as `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-reporting/workspace`.

## Bring a complete source collection into reporting

First finish or pause the desired source collection in the municipal operations workspace. Review its selected period, captured windows and any unresolved response-cap intervals. From **Source collections**, download the complete collection JSON, or use:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-operations \
  --collection COLLECTION_ID \
  --kind json \
  --out /absolute/handover/municipal-collection.json
```

The input is the complete `commons.open311.collection-export.v1` envelope. Keep that file unchanged. It contains the saved plan, every retained original capture, occurrence and source version, consolidated request selection, coverage summary and source operations. The reporting importer saves the original text and its content hash along with the parsed input.

Initialize a separate reporting workspace, then import the collection:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs init \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs state \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs import \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --file /absolute/handover/municipal-collection.json \
  --request-id municipal-source-intake-001 \
  --expected-revision 0
```

Use revision 0 only for a newly initialized empty workspace. For later mutations, read its current state and submit that exact revision. A saved request ID belongs to one complete input. If its response is lost, look up the operation and repeat the same ID, revision and input; prepare a new ID only for a new intended action.

You may import more than one complete collection. Reporting retains each source identity and each observed edition. Report definitions explicitly select the source IDs used for that report.

## Open the operator interface

Start the initialized reporting workspace:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 0
```

Open the private URL printed in the single JSON startup line. The server establishes the same-origin browser session when it serves the start page.

In merchant **Applications**, choose **Open311 service performance** and select the initialized reporting directory. The launcher reads the original `open311-reporting.sqlite` identity, starts the reporting command, and matches its live workspace ID, private directory binding and server instance. This keeps the opened application attached to the selected reporting workspace across ordinary merchant operations.

The browser workflow is:

1. **Sources:** import complete collection files and inspect their saved source identity and coverage.
2. **Rules:** save a named profile with a provider interpretation, exact source/status mappings, operator calendars and target policies.
3. **Build reports:** select source collections, a saved profile revision, an explicit reporting period and an as-of instant.
4. **Reports:** inspect totals, groups, individual source editions, calculated targets, calculation issues and management commentary; compare two saved reports.
5. **Reviewer returns:** import a returned review package, select the comments to apply and explicitly choose any report rebase.
6. **Workspace:** export the complete reporting workspace or receive a complete package into an initialized empty destination.

The browser retains the original mutation input before submitting it. Its recovery panel can inspect a saved operation, retry the exact original command and download that command for a later browser session. A revision conflict leaves the original command available while the operator prepares a corrected action against the current workspace.

## Save service rules and targets

A profile has its own ID and revision. Save a new revision when changing an existing operational policy so reports remain tied to the exact rules used to build them.

The basic editor covers:

- Source grouping rules with exact service, agency, status or request selectors.
- Display labels for original provider statuses.
- Named working calendars, weekly intervals, date overrides, time zone and daylight-saving disambiguation.
- Elapsed-time or business-time targets, their originating event and completion event.
- A separately configured interpretation of internal date-only review deadlines.
- Operator references and management notes.

The advanced JSON editor preserves the full profile structure for configurations that need more detailed selectors. Empty selectors are explicit rules covering all selected requests; give those rules a clear name and operator reference. Matching rules with equal priority are calculation issues to resolve, rather than an implicit choice of one rule.

Calendar hours, target durations and local deadlines are operator policies. Preserve their names, revisions and references. Use the source provider's documented semantics for source dates and statuses. In particular, Helsinki's latest-update time remains an update time and its native status remains visible beside any reporting label.

The source API can save the same complete profile file:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs profile \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --file /absolute/handover/service-profile.json \
  --request-id municipal-profile-001 \
  --expected-revision CURRENT_REVISION
```

Use the profile and report schemas in [README.md](./README.md) when creating files directly. The browser exports its full profile draft so its named settings can be inspected and saved through the same CLI.

## Build and compare reports

Each definition selects source IDs, an exact profile revision, a start-inclusive/end-exclusive requested-date period, an as-of instant, display time zone, target basis and optional group/status/review/assignee filters. Use ISO timestamps with explicit offsets for period boundaries and the as-of instant. The browser shows these values before saving a report.

Build from the complete definition file:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs build \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --file /absolute/handover/report-definition.json \
  --request-id municipal-report-001 \
  --expected-revision CURRENT_REVISION
```

Saved reports keep the original selected rows, source version hashes, target calculations, issues, coverage and commentary. Their source view shows the capture and source selection used for each case. Review an unresolved cap interval or unavailable source date in that context.

Use a stable series ID for related reporting periods. Compare two saved reports by their IDs:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs compare \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --before EARLIER_REPORT_ID \
  --after LATER_REPORT_ID
```

The definition and profile revision remain available beside the comparison. A difference in source selection, provider interpretation or target rules affects how the two periods should be read.

## Export reports and exchange reviewer comments

Export a saved report in HTML, CSV or complete JSON. The HTML report is suitable for printing or sharing. A JSON report package preserves the complete reporting workspace with the selected report ID, so the receiver gets its original sources, profile editions, report history and reviewer returns together.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --report REPORT_ID \
  --kind html \
  --out /absolute/handover/service-report.html

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --report REPORT_ID \
  --kind review \
  --out /absolute/handover/service-review.json
```

A review package names its base report and hash. It carries report comments and request comments; request comments identify the exact source key and source version. Give each returned change its own ID and identify the reviewer. The recipient imports the original returned file, inspects the changes and chooses the change IDs to apply.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs review-import \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --file /absolute/handover/service-review-return.json \
  --request-id municipal-review-intake-001 \
  --expected-revision CURRENT_REVISION

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/reporting/cli.mjs review-apply \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --file /absolute/handover/review-selection.json \
```

```sh
  --workspace /absolute/private/received-municipal-reporting \
```

Choose an empty destination. The complete reporting package carries imported original source text, profiles, saved reports and reviewer returns. Open the received directory with the same `serve` command or choose it in merchant Applications.

For browser receiving, initialize an empty destination, open its reporting interface and select **Workspace → Receive complete workspace**. The import uses that destination's current revision and retains the original receive command. The initialized destination keeps its own workspace identity. Its source records, profiles, reports and reviewer returns come from the received package, and the original workspace identity and operations remain recorded in its receiving history.

Retain the original collection workspace separately when continuing civic-source acquisition. Each subsequent complete collection export is a new explicit reporting intake; existing reports remain tied to their saved inputs.
